content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?EarthSky's PostEarthSkyApril 1 at 11:01 PM · Shared with PublicThe Artemis 2 mission with 4 brave astronauts on board lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center at 6:35 p.m. EDT on Wednesday. The Space Launch System propelled the Orion crew capsule from historic launch complex 39B in Florida into space, where the crew will be the first to fly around the moon since the final Apollo mission in 1972. It will take approximately 4 days for the spaceship to reach the moon. The Artemis 2 mission will not land, but will spend 10 days in space, in preparation for future missions to land and eventually build a moon base.Read more about #Artemis 2 at https://earthsky.org/.../the-artemis-program-nasas.../ Greg Diesel Walck.All reactions:881121 comments83 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Shelley BeardsleyI remember watching the Apollo launch to the moon with Neil Armstrong as making the first step on the moon.
